items.summary: Which biological findings enter a reported explanation depends on how the model population was constructed, a choice predictive validation alone does not reveal. We fitted 10,000 L2-regularised logistic regression models to TCGA pan-cancer tumour-versus-normal data: 100 regularisation strengths on 100 train-test splits, with patients fixed within each split. Strongly and weakly regularised models differ in mean accuracy by only 0.21 percentage points, yet prioritise different genes systematically with regularisation strength. Averaging explanations across a hyperparameter grid produces a top-50 panel sharing 41 genes with a single fitted model, but which model depends on the grid centre (Spearman correlation 0.92, 350 simulated practitioners). For 43 of 50 practitioners, the panel combines genes from strongly and weakly regularised models more fully than any fitted model: the explanation belongs to no model whose accuracy was established. A conventional grid recovers only a quarter of genes favoured exclusively by the strongest regularisation. HMGCS2 ranks among the top 50 in 73 of 100 strongly regularised fits and no weakly regularised fits, yet appears in none of 50 simulated reports. Reconstructing a published biomarker workflow on 20 cohort resamples reveals a different failure: the closest refit contains only 23 of the averaged panel's 50 genes, and no panel gene appears in all 20 refits. We define model-relative provenance as how much of a panel any single fitted model contains, distinct from workflow provenance recording how an analysis was run. We provide measurements to make the model population, the choice that selects from it, and that provenance reportable.
items.title: Same Accuracy, Different Gene Panels: How the Hyperparameter Grid Chooses the Reported Explanation

items.summary: Sixteen commits since v1.0.0 (2026-07-05). The pipeline was run end to end for the first time on the current Claude Science product in this window — ComputationalReviewSSTdisease — and most of what follows comes from defects that run exposed. Runtime Runs with nothing to install: the coordinator saves skills/*.md as artifacts at session start and hands sub-agents the skill files they need (new "Runtime: Claude Science" section in the orchestrator). LITREVIEW and DATAML are roles delegated to default sub-agents, not profiles. Legacy delegate_to / operon.* / pipeline.* calls updated to host.* (#5). All 20 skills carry name / description frontmatter. Fixes found by running the pipeline Authorship widget published empty. The Phase 14 instruction said :authors: ../authors.yml ; the plugin resolves that path relative to the document directory, and 00_frontmatter.md and authors.yml both live in content/ . Corrected to ./authors.yml , with the silent-failure mode documented (#5). Evidence Database page published empty from a complete evidence set, with a green build. Four independent faults: the plugin never followed the v29 evidence_section_NN.json rename, looped sections 02..13 , read argument_groups.*.supporting_findings cite-key strings as finding records, and swallowed every read failure in catch { continue } . It now discovers the section files present, accepts all three historical naming conventions, prefers ev.findings , and throws rather than publishing empty (#6). Build failed on an un-instantiated evidence directory. A directory with no JSON at all is now treated as a template awaiting a run and renders a placeholder; JSON present but matching no package name stays fatal (#8). comprev-scoping.md 's description frontmatter was truncated mid-sentence (#5). Version management The pipeline generation number lived in a filename and in ~20 loose strings, while the only release tag described itself as "Expert Review Pipeline v29". The generation now lives solely in skills/manifest.json , which also records the sha256 and byte count of every skill file; the release version lives solely in git tags and is written into no file (#7). scripts/build_skill_manifest.py generates and verifies the manifest — standard library only — and a Skill manifest workflow runs --check on every push and pull request. It fails on a skill edited without a manifest regeneration, a version-bearing skill filename, a frontmatter name that disagrees with its filename, a description quoting the wrong generation, or a README naming a generation the manifest does not. Session setup writes provenance/pipeline_version.json into each review (generation, template commit, template tag, manifest hash, per-skill artifact ids). Phase 1's review_request.md header, Methods M.8 and pipeline_metrics.json read the version from that file instead of carrying a typed-in number. Renamed skills/comprev-orchestrator-v29.md → skills/comprev-orchestrator.md . Update saved prompts that name the old path. Nothing depends on this repository programmatically, and reviews already produced carry their own copy of skills/ , so they are unaffected.

items.summary: This dataset provides computational supplements, source code, finite-state component data, and independently checkable BFACF certificates for Makoto Ozawa, "Merge Trees of Length-Filtered Lattice Knot Spaces" (arXiv:2605.25322). The data concern self-avoiding polygons in the simple cubic lattice under standard BFACF moves and a lattice-length filtration. The earlier release documents the complete minimal-layer merge trees of $4_1$ (four components at length 30 merging at length 32) and $6_3$ (twelve components at length 40, two at length 42, and one at length 44). It also documents selected nonminimal trefoil components born at length 26; these selected births are not claimed to exhaust the full filtered graph. The frozen-unknot construction consists of a 64-edge Hamiltonian lattice unknot with no length-preserving or length-decreasing BFACF moves. An independently verified sequence of 25,436 BFACF moves reduces it to the elementary square with peak length 66. A two-edge block-splicing construction gives frozen unknots of length $64m$ for every integer $m\ge1$. New in the 19 October 2026 update: A minimal 24-edge trefoil is spliced to the 64-edge frozen unknot to produce an explicit 88-edge trefoil admitting no length-nonincreasing BFACF moves. The additional files supply the lattice direction words and coordinates, connected-sum construction, local-move verifier, and sampled checks for $m=1,2,3,4,8,16$. Repeating the frozen unknot block before the final trefoil splice gives frozen trefoils of length $64m+24$ for every $m\ge1$; reflection gives both chiralities. The results imply infinitely many nonminimal strong local-minimum births for the unknot and for both trefoil chiralities, within the standard BFACF filtration. The exact merge height 66 is established only for the 64-edge unknot. For longer frozen unknots and trefoils the proofs give lower bounds $H(P_m,U)\ge64m+2$ and $H(R_m,Q)\ge64m+26$, respectively; no exact merge heights or unbounded minimax excess are claimed. The construction is discrete and does not establish a positive barrier in continuous ropelength-filtered knot spaces or a universal result for arbitrary knot types. The archive retains earlier datasets and provenance information. Reproducibility instructions identify which outputs come from complete finite enumeration, certified BFACF paths, protected-port constructions, or limited computational checks.
tags: Lattice knots; BFACF moves; merge trees; strong local minima; Gordian unknots; Hamiltonian lattice p

items.summary: This reproducibility package accompanies the study “Grain-Scale Radiation Transport and the Robustness of Radiolytic H₂–Sulfate Imbalance in the Revell Crystalline-Rock System.” The study evaluates how radiation-specific grain-scale transport modifies radiolytic H₂ and sulfate production estimates in the low-porosity Revell crystalline-rock system and tests the robustness of the inferred H₂–sulfate production imbalance. The package contains processed and derived data, analysis and transport-model code, computational notebooks, source data for the main figures, frozen manuscript-level results, and reproducibility metadata. Grain-scale α- and β-radiation transport is evaluated over a grain-diameter sensitivity domain of 0.06–2000 μm, while γ transport and post-interface energy partitioning are treated through explicit sensitivity bounds. The package supports reproduction and audit of the numerical results and figures reported in the associated manuscript. Third-party source datasets are not redistributed as original research data in this archive. Their provenance, persistent identifiers, and access information are documented so that the computational workflow can be traced to the original sources. Research-generated data, figures, and documentation are released under CC BY 4.0, while original research code in the package is released under the MIT License.
items.title: Grain-Scale Radiation Transport and the Robustness of Radiolytic H₂–Sulfate Imbalance in the Revell Crystalline-Rock System

It constructs a protected positive-energy non-luminous sector, a distinct collective saturation mechanism, an internally owned late-sector abundance map, and an effective collisionless astronomical closure linking the same dark-state dynamics to gravitational and lensing observables. items.summary: This computational package accompanies the Neuro-Symbolic MAPE-K governance testbed for agentic retrieval-augmented generation at the edge. It provides Python source, experimental inputs, measured outputs, provenance manifests, analysis tables, figures and readable evidence reports for two related campaigns: the October 2026 MAPE-K controller campaign and the separate 18 October 2026 dense-retriever control campaign. The retriever control records 3,744 retrieval trials and 640 clean-validation query evaluations across sparse, pretrained dense and clean-fitted dense retrievers. It performs no new generator or controller evaluation. The package preserves campaign-specific directory layouts and historical execution records. A dependency-light deterministic template smoke test supports inspection without language-model downloads or CUDA. Full inference and fitting used NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX 8 GB and platform-specific CUDA/PyTorch environments. Original host paths and observed package inventories are provenance records, not a universal portable lockfile; full main-campaign model weights are referenced by revision and checksum, while the retriever campaign includes its pretrained and clean-fitted checkpoints. A release verifier checks the curated file manifest and metadata. The original retrieval verifier also requires original source paths for its final host-specific integrity checks. Original project software is MIT licensed (SPDX: MIT), with collective copyright held by the MAPE-K contributors. Third-party terms remain applicable: O*NET 31.0 and UCI Adult-derived data and fixtures are CC BY 4.0 with attribution and modification notices; MiniLM model material and its clean-fitted derivative are Apache-2.0; BGE model material and its clean-fitted derivative are MIT with upstream attribution. File-specific notices, exact model revisions and checksums are retained. Experimental counts reuse base profiles and should not be interpreted as independent efficacy replications. The evidence does not establish population fairness, human-validated answer-quality superiority, or a guarantee of safe retrieved evidence.

items.summary: INTEGRATED PHOTONIC MICROROBOTIC SYSTEMS AT THE LIMIT FLAGSHIP 16 / 30 | STARLI RESEARCH INSTITUTE XXIV This prospective research monograph investigates whether silicon-photonic light distribution, optofluidic packaging, independent metrology, and feedback positioning can be integrated into a compact research station that reliably captures, transports, releases, and recovers microscopic proxy agents. Its central hypothesis is system-level rather than decorative: reducing external optics is a meaningful advance only when delivered optical power, fluid transport, sample heating, task outcomes, and failure responses remain independently observable and reproducible across fabricated chip and package lots. The study develops a five-layer research architecture encompassing packaged optical and fluidic paths; a physically bounded optical-power and thermal ledger; external tracking capable of challenging on-chip estimates; reversible multi-agent tasks under staged fault injection; and repair, requalification, cost, and cross-laboratory transfer. It separates electromagnetic optical force from thermal convection, surface adhesion, Brownian motion, and sensor-induced artefacts. Strong comparators include calibrated free-space optical tweezers and spatial-light-modulator trapping configurations at matched specimen exposure and operational throughput. The book contains 30 mathematics-linked derivational routes, 82 chapters with 410 independently paginated research sections, 200 detailed future Research Gates, and 33 provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos. A companion Excel atlas links each research chapter, quantitative candidate, test protocol, falsifier and external DOI evidence record. Publisher-identified publications on integrated optical phased arrays, silicon-photonic trapping, and photonics packaging inform the research boundary but are not treated as proof that the integrated microrobotic platform proposed here has already been demonstrated. The primary design principle is independent reproducibility: a controller should never be allowed to certify its own sensor output, ignore lost agents, or authorize a restart after a failed optical-power or thermal ledger. Negative studies, matched classical successes, and failed module integrations are retained as useful successor research evidence. This work offers testable possibilities for future investigation; it is not a claim of experimentally demonstrated autonomous nanorobots, and it has not undergone external peer review.

items.summary: This working paper consolidates the mathematical correspondences studied between selected string-theory models and the Phase framework of the Harmonic Physics research programme. It presents the central equations, reported evidence and outstanding physical questions, with detailed derivations, controls and computational records retained in companion reports and reproducibility packages. A compact phase field reproduces the momentum–winding contribution of the declared circle-compactified bosonic closed-string model and preserves that contribution under reciprocal exchange of radius, momentum and winding. A quadratic optical continuation retains a reciprocal canonical description and yields a dispersion relation containing quadratic and quartic wave-number terms. A retrospective comparison with released fluid-of-light measurements favors inclusion of the retained gradient within the scope of the processed experimental records. For a specified two-component continuum action with fixed component amplitudes, constant coefficients and equal propagation speeds, the relative phase obeys an exact sine-Gordon equation, while the common phase obeys a free wave equation. This conditional classical correspondence applies at finite relative-phase excursion and connects to the equation obtained through Pohlmeyer reduction of classical bosonic strings on R_t × S². The assumptions and remaining reconstruction questions are stated explicitly. A separate conditional gravity construction maps a fixed source coefficient into a supplied Schwarzschild exterior compatible with the leading string metric condition. The construction retains explicit assumptions about spatial geometry, dimensional calibration and vacuum dynamics. The master also discusses polarization-dependent apparent position and identifies a predictive relationship between foundational Phase, observer coupling and registered distance as a continuing research question. The paper distinguishes the established mathematical correspondences and bounded optical-model evidence from the proposed foundational interpretation of Phase. Physical identification, reconstruction of the evolved breather with the required global string conditions, and quantum equivalence are not established by the reported comparisons. Version and update policy This is a living research document, updated as further mathematical derivations, correspondences and reproducible tests are completed. Future substantive revisions will be released as new numbered Zenodo versions, accompanied by a dated summary of changes. Please cite the specific version consulted. Version 0.21 — 19 October 2026: Added the seven giant-magnon benchmarks and their amplitude–phase correspondences, distinguishing classical results from the narrower semiclassical result. Detailed methods, results and reproducibility materials are documented in the companion publication, Giant Magnon Amplitude and Phase Correspondences : https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23463422 . Keywords: String theory, Harmonic Physics, Phase dynamics, Phase nesting, Mathematical correspondence, Compact scalar fields, Compactification, Momentum and winding, T-duality, Sine-Gordon equation, Pohlmeyer reduction, Canonical transformations, Optical dispersion, Fluids of light, Schwarzschild geometry, Observer coupling, Optical localization, Reproducible research
items.title: String Theory and Phase: Mathematical Correspondence and Current Interpretation

items.summary: Reproducible and analytically robust research findings are essential to scientific progress, but evaluating these properties typically requires costly manual effort. We investigate whether LLM agents can help automate reproduction and robustness analysis, using a medical case study grounded in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, a widely used U.S. cancer registry underlying tens of thousands of published studies. First, we introduce SEER-Repro, a benchmark of 20 published SEER-based papers together with the data and resources required to reproduce their findings. Second, we create an AI agent that successfully reproduces 77.4% of 2,190 atomic claims, while providing executable baselines for further analysis. Third, we develop an agentic analysis pipeline to test the robustness of the medical findings by identifying analytical choices underlying each finding, proposing defensible alternatives, and rerunning the analysis to determine whether those choices affect the conclusion. Across published papers in SEER-Repro, our pipeline identifies potentially consequential analytical choices in 9.5% of fully reproduced findings and flags them for expert review. These results show how LLM agents can support scientific review by reproducing findings, systematically testing their robustness, and directing expert attention toward potentially consequential analytical choices.
items.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery

items.summary: Oscilloscope probe compensation kits circulate between teaching laboratories, yet the calibration status of a kit is rarely transferred with the same rigour as the instrument it serves. the present analysis treats cross-course calibration transfer as a metrological problem and evaluates, by round-robin design, how bandwidth attenuation in a probe kit propagates into measurement discrepancy bounds when the kit is moved between courses. The evaluation is a replication-based characterisation of the before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64), with power estimated across 2000 design cells at cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points.54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect falls steeply as cluster count rises from 8 to 32. A first-order attenuation model links probe bandwidth to the fractional amplitude error at the test frequency, and the round-robin design is shown to bound the transfer discrepancy that a receiving course can expect. The contribution is a design-level calibration-transfer protocol that makes the discrepancy bound explicit before a kit leaves its home course, rather than after a student records a suspect waveform.
tags: probe compensation; calibration transfer; round-robin evaluation; bandwidth attenuation; measurement
items.title: Cross-Course Calibration Transfer of Oscilloscope Probe Compensation Kits in Engineering Education: A Round-Robin Evaluation Linking Bandwidth Attenuation to Measurement Discrepancy Bounds

For longer frozen unknots and trefoils the proofs give lower bounds $H(P_m,U)\ge64m+2$ and $H(R_m,Q)\ge64m+26$, respectively; no exact merge heights or unbounded minimax excess are claimed. The construction is discrete and does not establish a positive barrier in continuous ropelength-filtered knot spaces or a universal result for arbitrary knot types. The archive retains earlier datasets and provenance information. Reproducibility instructions identify which outputs come from complete finite enumeration, certified BFACF paths, protected-port constructions, or limited computational checks.

items.summary: Student-built load banks used in undergraduate electrical machines laboratories typically derive rotor speed from a slotted-disc tachometer whose pulse train is quantised by a fixed sampling clock, and the resulting slip estimate feeds directly into the torque-speed curve that students report. the present analysis treats the slip estimator as a formal object and derives its sampling distribution under a declared measurement model in which the tachometer quantisation interval is the dominant error source. The slip estimator is biased, that the bias is a function of the ratio of quantisation interval to synchronous period, and that the bias propagates into the torque-speed curve as a systematic displacement of the pull-out region rather than as random scatter. A replication-based evaluation was conducted: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2), and the ordinary least squares estimator was characterised under the stated process. The estimated bias for the intercept was -0.02315 and for the exposure coefficient 0.00064; the root mean squared errors were 0.88484 and 0.01581 respectively; empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that the estimator is essentially unbiased for the slope but that the intercept carries a small negative displacement, and that the quantisation mechanism identified analytically is consistent with the direction and magnitude of the observed intercept bias. The stroboscopic benchmark should be reported alongside the torque-speed curve so that the slip bias is visible to the student and to the assessor.

items.summary: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our DiscoveryRSI framework develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable Harbor tasks, and recursively learns through three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization attributes scientific assessments to documented research contributions; harness replay identifies productive strategies and recurring failures to refine research workflows; and rediscovery applies accepted improvements to new investigations, generating further experience for subsequent learning. We also introduce DFM-Bench, which provides comprehensive assessment of hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress at the levels of hypotheses, revisions, development paths and research runs. Across four life-science domains, automated evaluation shows that hypothesis quality rises from 4.86 for the base model to 5.39 after two rounds of self-improvement, with the large gains in falsifiability and data resolvability. We further validate hypothesis quality through expert review, comparing our DiscoveryRSI-27B with other research agents. Preliminary human assessments show that DiscoveryRSI-27B scores higher than GPT-6 Luna on hypothesis importance and whether claims are plausible and evidence-bounded. DiscoveryRSI-27B achieved a 6.3% rate of hypothesis correspondence with research published after the model cutoff, largely outperform GPT-6 with 2.5% and Claude Opus 5 with 2.3%, while delivering greater human-rated improvement along research paths.
items.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses

items.summary: Emergency-stop circuits built by engineering technology students are routinely treated as safe once they pass a functional test at commissioning, yet the relay contact welding that dominates their failure modes is invisible to such tests and accumulates silently across the workshop's operating life. The framework represents a student-built circuit as a series safety function whose integrity is degraded by contact welding, and derives the conditions under which a welded contact converts a demanded stop into an undetected loss of safety function. A replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator was conducted under a declared variance structure with a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.64, across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The evaluation indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect at 80% power falls as the number of clusters rises. The framework proposes that workshop safety assurance should shift from commissioning-time functional testing to integrity monitoring that is sensitive to contact welding, and the design analysis implies that cluster-level evaluations of such interventions require cluster counts well above those typical of single-institution studies.

items.summary: In autonomous driving, perceiving surrounding objects is not enough: failing to understand how they move and interact over time can lead to dangerous decisions. Evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) therefore requires testing whether they connect past spatial observations to future consequences. Yet existing benchmarks often assess edge cases through basic perception questions or test temporal understanding in simple scenarios, leaving complex spatiotemporal reasoning underexplored. We introduce STRIDE (SpatioTemporal Reasoning In Driving Edge Cases), an object-centric benchmark for long-tail, safety-critical driving scenarios. STRIDE covers six task families: spatial perception, spatial understanding, temporal memory, temporal extrapolation, trajectory prediction, and scene-context awareness. It pairs multiple-choice questions probing individual spatiotemporal judgments with related free-form visual question answering (VQA) requiring detailed scene explanations and justifications of driving decisions. We prioritize scenes with unusual object behaviors and complex traffic interactions, generate reference answers from structured dataset annotations through automated procedures, and use limited language-model assistance and human verification to ensure annotation quality. Across 12 proprietary, open-weight, and driving-specialized models, even the best performer, GPT-6-Astra, achieves only 43.4% average multiple-choice accuracy, versus an approximately 20% random-choice baseline. Further analysis reveals that strong performance in describing driving scenes does not necessarily translate to accurate safety-critical judgments, and that models struggle more with reconstructing object motion than recalling past positions. STRIDE thus exposes spatiotemporal driving limitations that aggregate VQA scores can conceal.
items.title: STRIDE: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Driving Edge Cases

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent outputs that lack source support or conflict with local operational constraints. We introduce Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT), a modular architecture that organizes generation as a closed Retrieve--Reflect--Revise loop. SRCoT separates environment state, persistent knowledge, accumulated experience, and short-term memory into provenance-labeled stores. BM25 retrieval supplies local context; subsequent passes expose intermediate drafts, missing-information markers, follow-up queries, and optional claim--evidence mappings. These artifacts inform retrieval, revision, clarification, or abstention decisions. We examine the architecture through qualitative, trace-based case studies in two fully synthetic settings: emergency medical services and Munich-Sim, an emergency-operations simulation. Local prototype runs on an Apple M4-family laptop with 128 GB memory illustrate source-labeled documentation, explicit gap marking, and structured dispatch-style outputs. The traces also reveal provenance-assignment errors, incomplete evidence coverage, and unsafe assumptions that remain possible despite prompting constraints. These cases demonstrate report-level inspectability and local execution, not comparative superiority, hallucination reduction, clinical validity, or operational safety. The architecture separates retrieval and control from the model interface, but behavior across different models remains to be evaluated. SRCoT is a research proof of concept requiring human review, with its principal contribution lying in an inspectable control procedure rather than a new model.
items.title: Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT): Evidence-Based Text Generation via a Closed-Loop Retrieve--Reflect--Revise Pipeline on Edge LLMs

items.summary: LLM-agent memory selection often uses retrieval rankings based on record relevance or individual influence. Such rankings cannot identify sufficient subsets under redundant or jointly necessary evidence. We study per-decision memory sufficiency: selecting a small subset that preserves full-memory behavior. To separate search error from model error, we introduce JointCoreBench, a benchmark with nine interaction families, six workflow domains, natural-language decisions, and exact sufficient-set oracles, and JointCore, a relevance cost-ordered group-deletion baseline that tests blocks before individual records. On 6,912 exact conditions, cost-ordered JointCore recovers a minimum-cost sufficient set in 100.0% of cases, reduces subset evaluations from 30.00 to 11.13 (62.9%), and achieves 87.8% active-memory savings. Across four 12B-70B model families and 432 tasks per model, its unweighted mean is 10.28 versus 16.00 model queries and 50.6% versus 43.1% minimum-cost recovery relative to cost aware singleton deletion. Both methods preserve full-memory behavior under the deterministic primary interface. Tests with physical deletion, UNKNOWN masks, PENDING sentinels, counterfactual values, and alternative labels identify interface dependent behavior. JointCore is an efficient benchmark baseline; the study does not establish deployment-ready memory compression.
items.title: Beyond Marginal Influence: Interaction-Aware Memory Selection for LLM Agents

items.summary: Algorithmic systems increasingly allocate tasks, rank performance, flag anomalies, and recommend decisions that affect employment conditions. This critical integrative review examines how algorithmic management may reshape employee voice and perceptions of procedural justice in AI-assisted organizations. It distinguishes automated recommendations from fully automated decisions, information disclosure from effective contestability, and worker participation from symbolic consultation. Established research on algorithmic control, organizational justice, algorithmic transparency, and human-AI decision structures provides the conceptual basis. The article develops an accountability chain linking data provenance, decision rights, reviewability, employee explanation, correction pathways, and evaluation of organizational outcomes. It argues that the mere presence of a human reviewer does not demonstrate meaningful oversight; review authority, adequate information, and the ability to change an outcome are separate requirements. Potential benefits of automation include consistency and early detection of harmful errors, while risks include opaque sanctions, strategic data manipulation, and the displacement of responsibility. No primary interviews, experimental observations, or quantitative effect estimates are reported. The proposed empirical agenda combines process tracing, employee surveys, decision-log audits, scenario-based experiments, and organizational comparisons. The framework can be supported only if its specified safeguards improve measurable fairness, accuracy, employee trust, and organizational performance beyond existing governance practices. algorithmic management; employee voice; procedural justice; AI governance; human oversight; organizational accountability
items.title: Algorithmic Management, Employee Voice, and Procedural Justice: A Governance Framework for Accountable AI-Assisted Organizations

items.summary: Quantum kernels are among the most promising methods in quantum machine learning, providing a natural way to embed data into high-dimensional Hilbert spaces via quantum circuits and capturing non-linear relationships in data. Their learning behaviour is governed by the function class they represent, which is formally characterized by the structure of the associated Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS). However, a theoretical characterization of this function class, and of how it depends on the choice of feature map and its hyperparameters, is still lacking. In this work, we focus on the Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial (IQP) feature map and derive a Fourier representation of the associated RKHS generators as finite sums of trigonometric functions evaluated on polynomially transformed input variables, with a finite set of accessible frequencies determined by the circuit construction and scaled by the bandwidth hyperparameter. This representation identifies three bandwidth regimes with qualitatively distinct expressive properties from localised, through multimodal, to periodic. Numerical experiments on synthetic datasets with controlled periodic and multimodal structure, across data dimensions and feature-map configurations, reproduce the three regimes in both supervised classification and unsupervised anomaly detection, benchmarked against a classical Gaussian kernel. These results make the relationship between expressivity and data structure explicit for IQP kernels: expressive power translates into a practical benefit only when the accessible frequencies match with the structure of the data, which provides a criterion for selecting the bandwidth when the periodic or multimodal structure of data is known.
items.title: Expressivity of IQP Feature-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces

items.summary: Lyapunov exponents (LEs) are fundamental metrics from nonlinear dynamical systems theory that quantify the average exponential rate of divergence or convergence of nearby trajectories in phase space. Over the past three decades, LEs have emerged as powerful tools across a wide range of power system problems, including transient and voltage stability assessment, chaos detection and mitigation, short-term load and renewable energy forecasting, and fault diagnosis. This paper presents a comprehensive review of these applications, covering more than 165 publications spanning from the early demonstrations of chaos in simplified machine models (1990s) to the most recent data-driven and machine-learning-augmented approaches applied to inverter-based resource (IBR)-dominated grids (2024--2026). The review is organized into four principal application domains: (i) stability analysis and real-time monitoring, (ii) chaos characterization and control, (iii) forecasting and predictability analysis, and (iv) protection, fault diagnosis, and condition monitoring. For each domain, we trace the evolution of methods, compare model-based and data-driven LE estimation strategies, identify key benchmarks and validation gaps, and outline the most pressing open research problems.
items.title: Lyapunov Exponents in Power Systems: A Survey of Theory and Applications in Stability, Control, Forecasting, and Protection

Every figure and analysis tunable lives in the settings JSON and is documented; notebooks load imports in cell 1 and settings in cell 2. Stored keys renamed with legacy readers: call_type -> vocal_class , n_calls -> n_vocalizations . root_directory is required by the processing classes; first_match_or_raise raises on more than one match. Results to recompute Inter-USV interval archives and K selections; manifold selections and univariate manifold runs (20 folds); onset, behavioural-response and matched-divergence extractions; coactivity results; GLM-HMM log-likelihood/BIC columns; the behaviour-control artifact and nested decoding; gating and vocal-decoding sections; QLVM training sets built with the old exclusion; summaries built with the consensus remerge ( chs_count ).

items.summary: Relational out-of-distribution errors are easy to describe and hard to evaluate cleanly. An image may be natural, a caption may be fluent, and all mentioned objects may be common, yet the caption may describe the wrong relation in the image. Many evaluations intended to test this behavior can be solved without checking the pairing at all, because negatives differ in caption style, template, length, object frequency, or image statistics. We propose counterfactual pairing cycles, a blocked evaluation primitive that reuses the same two images and the same two captions on both sides of the comparison, changing only which image is paired with which caption. This makes image-only, text-only, and additive component shortcuts cancel exactly in finite samples. The same contrast also gives a training loss for relational outlier exposure and a diagnostic for bilinear vision-language scores. Across synthetic controls, GQA, and COCO, cycles separate coarse image-caption matching from directional role-binding failures, while also identifying geometric size relations that remain strongly visible in global features. In a shortcut-contaminated COCO outlier-exposure stress test, a model selected by a near-perfect shortcut validation AUROC retains substantial relational signal but remains below cycle training on exact cycles; cycle training improves CycleAcc from 0.882 to 0.927. The main lesson is simple: to test whether a model understands a pairing, the benchmark should keep the parts fixed, change the pairing, and ask only about coupling. The official implementation is available online.
items.title: Can the Parts Fool the Test? Counterfactual Pairing Cycles for Relational OOD

items.summary: Recent large audio language models (LALMs) have extended their capabilities beyond lexical speech understanding to tasks requiring paralinguistic and non-linguistic audio understanding, such as emotion recognition. However, these models still struggle to reliably utilize acoustic information, particularly when it co-occurs with spoken linguistic content. Existing benchmarks do not clearly distinguish acoustic perception from higher-level reasoning, making it difficult to identify the source of these failures. To address this issue, we introduce VocalGrad, a benchmark designed to evaluate LALMs' ability to perceive low-level acoustic variations. VocalGrad formulates this problem as a simple binary classification of temporal change direction, enabling evaluation largely independent of higher-level reasoning or semantic understanding. Our benchmark results reveal a substantial gap in acoustic perception between human annotators and state-of-the-art LALMs: while human annotators achieve high accuracy, LALMs perform at near-chance levels. We further conduct linear probing to identify structural bottlenecks in these models. Our analysis reveals two distinct failure modes: for some categories, task-relevant information is preserved in internal representations but not utilized by the language model head; for others, the information becomes progressively less linearly decodable across model layers. Overall, our results reveal substantial limitations of LALMs in modeling acoustic variation under controlled settings and expose representation differences not observable from text outputs.
items.title: VocalGrad: Evaluating Acoustic Perception in Audio Language Models

items.summary: Modern deep learning systems increasingly rely on high-dimensional vector operations, in which large input and parameter vectors are repeatedly stored, transferred, and processed. Although substantial research has focused on reducing neural-network model size through pruning, quantization, knowledge distillation, and efficient architectures, the storage, memory-traffic, and communication costs associated with repeatedly presented high-dimensional input vectors remain important practical considerations, particularly in distributed and edge-computing environments. This paper proposes the SETAREH (Sorting-assisted Energy-concentrating Transform for Approximate Representation using Haar wavelets) transform, a Haar-wavelet-based sparsification approach for approximating the inner product between a fixed high-dimensional coefficient vector and successive input vectors. By applying the same sequence of permutations and Haar transforms to both vectors, SETAREH preserves the exact inner product before truncation. It then retains only a subset of the transformed coefficient-input pairs, reducing their representation cost while introducing a controllable approximation error. To evaluate SETAREH, we consider two complementary experimental settings: a synthetic Gaussian-vector baseline and a real apparent-age estimation task using a convolutional neural network on the APPA-REAL dataset. The results show that SETAREH can approximate the evaluated inner products using substantially fewer transformed coefficient-input pairs than the original vector dimension. The findings support its use as a potential structured data-representation method for repeated inner products with fixed weights, while the practical benefit depends on approximation accuracy and the cost of storing or transmitting permutation metadata.
items.title: SETAREH Transform: A Sorting-Assisted Haar-Wavelet Sparsification Method for Approximate Inner-Product Computation

items.summary: Research compendium for the article "Climate warming is projected to reduce and redistribute Aedes albopictus abundance, away from Po Valley hotspots towards Alpine margins" (M. C. Darılmaz, Science of the Total Environment; manuscript STOTEN-D-26-01129R1). The study predicts weekly ovitrap egg counts of the Asian tiger mosquito at 149 monitoring stations in Italy, Albania, Switzerland and France (VectAbundance, 2010–2022). The framework has four layers: a mechanistic life-history model (dynamAedes 2.2.9); gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost) and random forests with climate, remote-sensing, land-use, demographic and population-genetic predictors; an ablation of the population-genetic layer; and projections under 48 CMIP6 combinations (four General Circulation Models, three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways, four periods to 2100). The archive contains: - 48 Python, 8 R and 1 Google Earth Engine scripts, with PIPELINE.md giving the order in which they run; - the processed station-level data and the final modelling tables (42,118 station–week records), with the station-to-fold assignment used by every cross-validated analysis; - the trained XGBoost and Random Forest models with their cross-validation predictions, feature importance and SHAP values; - the outputs of the ablation and sensitivity analyses: mechanistic and genetic ablations, genetic structure versus geographic position, fold-count sensitivity, fold-level inference, feature correlation and VIF, spatio-temporal and leave-one-year-out cross-validation, remote-sensing gap-filling, baseline period, calibration and validation detail, treatment of the year predictor, inputs that carry the projected change, and the fill of weeks without mechanistic output; - the inputs and outputs of the 48-scenario projection, per climate model, as ensemble and at station level. Main results reproduced by the archive: cross-validated R² of the full model 0.534 ± 0.093 (XGBoost; pooled 0.539) and 0.544 ± 0.081 (Random Forest). Projected change in mean active-season abundance over the 12 SSP–period combinations: −4 to −27 % at Hot lowland stations (−6 to −44 % in the Po Valley) and +10 to +106 % at Cool upland and Alpine margin stations. Raw inputs that are publicly available from their primary archives (ERA5-Land, WorldClim 2.1 and its CMIP6 projections, satellite imagery, GHS-POP, the population-genetic source data and GenBank sequences) are not redistributed; README.md lists the sources and how the scripts locate them. items.title: Climate warming is projected to reduce and redistribute Aedes albopictus abundance, away from Po Valley hotspots towards Alpine margins
